blockers.blocker: hintikka_imp_pos / hintikka_imp_neg are unprovable AS STATED for Lukasiewicz-encoded connectives
blockers.root_cause: and/or/neg are encoded as nested imp: and = (phi->(psi->bot))->bot, or = (phi->bot)->psi, neg = phi->bot. modalApplyOne's tryAllPropRules pattern-matches the ENCODED connective with rule order [andPos,andNeg,orPos,orNeg,impPos,impNeg,negPos,negNeg]. So T((phi->(psi->bot))->bot) matches andPos FIRST and produces linear [pos phi w, pos psi w]. But hintikka_imp_pos claims conclusion 'neg a w in b OR pos c w in b' with a = phi->(psi->bot), c = bot. The and-rule output yields neither neg a nor pos c, so the bridge lemma is FALSE for conjunction/disjunction/negation-encoded inputs. modalTruthLemma calls hintikka_imp_pos/neg uniformly for EVERY Proposition.imp, including these encodings, so the factoring is unsound.
verified_mechanical_fixes_for_the_genuin: Per-case simp sets are MISSING Option.getD_some, so hcond stays a stuck 'match (if ...).fst with ...'. List.mem_cons_self is applied as 'List.mem_cons_self _ _' (two explicit args) but in this toolchain it takes NO explicit args (it IS the term 'a in a :: l'). Replace every 'List.mem_cons_self _ _' with 'List.mem_cons_self' in both imp lemmas.
